comment_text: Remove unrestricted parking on Highfield Lane
Not enough time to digest and/or discuss
Opposition to change of restrictions at St Denys Rd spur. Move the bus gate start north to the main junction
Bus stops are excessive in length- could be additional disabled parking or double yellows
Workshops not representative. Not enough families/children
Most signage does not show timings
“Bus gate ahead” sign on the Avenue?

TS14/15/10 mention “alternative route” without indicating alternative route to where. If Portswood you don’t need an alternative, if not Portswood then surely you are “through traffic” or “other routes”?
No base data or planned dates for data collection during the trial
Automatic Number Plate Recognition not included
Proposals are not safe
This effects local community and should not be actioned

I often pop into bitterne precinct for a few bits and bobs. If I had to pay to park I would definitely avoid and go elsewhere where I get free parking. People go to the gym nearby. By charging this might impact on people making healthy life choices as few people will want to pay for gym membership and then have to pay for parking 3-4 times a week. Bitterne precinct is having developments for a park. If you have to pay to park no one Is going to drive to bitterne to use the park (where they are likely to also pop into shops for a few things). Charging for parking wills seriously reduce the number of people coming and spending money in the bitterne area which will impact the local economy, community feel, people's fitness and wellbeing

It'll deter people from using local amenities, especially in Bitterne. Picking up from school will become more dangerous for children as parents park on surrounding streets. Church will lose collection money as congregants would have to pay to park. The gym would lose customers who will go elsewhere for free to park. Bitterne as a community will lose money as drivers will go elsewhere.

I Object to these proposals on the grounds that it is counter productive to local business. Why not take on the same approach as whitely with payment required over 4 hours? This will eliminate people leaving cars without deterring people visiting for short time periods and spending money (and VAT) in local shops. The 7 day enforcement until midnight is also a bit greedy in my opinion and a clear cash grab by the council from local residents. Enforcing these new rules in side streets and forcing residents to buy parking permits is also not fair on people who have lived and parked in the streets (which are already paid for through tax) for a long time
The one and only thing that Bitterne has, is free parking. It's not rocket science. People have cars and need to park and here is the one thing that draws them.

By removal of the free parking it will disuade people from visiting these areas and as such encourage people to shop in other areas. This in turn will drive decline in the financial revenue of these shops ultimately resulting in shop closures and a rapid decline in the shopping centre and footfall.

Ridiculous. It will kill off local shopping which is already suffering. What’s the point in spending money upgrading bitterne high street as no one will go there any more! Has anyone asked the opinions of shops in this area?
The shopping centre has already lost a lot of customers and parking charges will have a devastating affect on shopping around Southampton

We do a fair bit of our shopping in Bitterne because of it's free parking and because it is close, therefore low mileage. Less pollution and less cost. There is nothing there that we can't get elsewhere. Charges will make us probably go to Hedge End, (Village and Super Stores) where we can get virtually everything we can, at the moment, get in Bitterne. Why are you spending thousands of pounds refurbishing the area if you are going to discourage us from going there.

Free parking for two hours important to keep small local businesses going and to avoid more traffic in city centre or in out of town retail parks. Not everyone can walk or take the bus with heavy shopping or mobility issues.
This would stop me coming to local businesses

Considering that the car parks are used by residents on extremely low incomes for purposes of visiting health care sites etc, I think it’s wholly unfair and inappropriate to considering imposing these parking charges.
The council needs more money and people are obsessed with using cars for five minute nonsense trips. Make them get bikes I say.
